script.stored_text_completeness: All 19084 canonical characters read sequentially in full in 2 bounded ranges; auto-generated untimed text; stored ending is complete ("build your life."); ASR garbles ("F25" for F-250, "15 m per gallon", "$3.50 50 cents", "7.2% 2%", "Laram Longhorn", "Vevelin goods", "new workloads"); "You work in it" likely "You don't work in it"; audio, timed delivery and editing unverified.
script.opening_words: You're idling at a red light in your $87,000 Ford F-250 King Ranch Edition. The leather seats smell new. The dashboard glows like a spaceship. And when you roll past that Prius, you sit 6 in taller than everyone else on the road. You feel powerful. You feel capable. You feel like a man who can handle anything life throws at him. Except here's the thing. You work in it. Your job involves zero construction, zero farming, and zero towing.
script.ending_words: is clear. The truck is a trap. And the only way out is to stop pretending that burning $80,000 over seven years makes you more of a man. Real strength is looking at the numbers, admitting you've been sold a lie, and choosing the path that actually builds wealth instead of the one that just looks like it on Instagram. Buy the boring car, keep your money, build your life.
script.analysis: Full 19084 canonical characters read. A cost-teardown rant: hook ($87,000 F-250 King Ranch at a red light); channel pitch; purchase prices and median income; dealer payment over 84 months; fuel, insurance, tyres, maintenance, registration; total monthly cost; interest; used-Camry comparison; 7-year gap and invested alternative; DTI and housing; skipped vacation; emergency fund; credit-card spiral; relationship strain; career risk aversion; hedonic adaptation; parallel universes; "I use my truck" objection and U-Haul; marketing and dealers; boring-sedan prescription; depreciation myth; "I might need it"; Veblen goods; sell-it advice; close. Verified: Census 2024 median household income $83,730. Reproduces: fuel math, monthly sum, 7-year difference, emergency fund, card interest, depreciation. Wrong: interest ($14,748 vs ~$24,841), DTI (26% vs 17.6%), and several internally inconsistent totals ($73,836 vs "$83,000", "$80,000-120,000", "$40,000"; $1,247/$450 vs $1,100/$350). Most cost increments are assumptions. The stored ending is complete.
